end.summary:
- Interpreted position-time and velocity-time graphs as motion stories, not path drawings.
- Read x-t slope as velocity and calculated 30/10 = 3 m/s.
- Distinguished flat x-t (stopped) from flat v-t (constant velocity).
- Read v-t slope as acceleration and area as displacement; calculated 2.5 m/s² and 20 m.
- Teach-back was not passed; one v-t interpretation needed continued checking.
end.parentNote: Ira practised reading graphs as descriptions of motion rather than pictures of a road. They used slope for velocity or acceleration and area under a v-t graph for displacement, including calculations of 3 m/s, 2.5 m/s², and 20 m. They clearly corrected the mix-up that an upward graph means a rising value, not a road going uphill, and explained the different meanings of flat x-t and v-t lines. At home, ask them to describe one x-t and one v-t graph in words before calculating anything.
